text: you're paying for AI capability. But the real skill is knowing when to use which level of capability. Claude is not just one model. It gives you a set of models and each one has a different job. Let's look at the model lineup. Start with Sonnet. Claude Sonnet 5 is now the default model for free and pro users. It is also the model most people should use most of the time. Anthropic describes it as the most agentic Sonnet model yet. That means it is better at planning, using tools, following through on multi-step tasks and handling everyday knowledge work. Think drafting, summarizing, research synthesis, artifact review, coding and workflow automation. For most leadership tasks, Sonnet is the right starting point. It gives you a strong balance of speed, quality and cost. Then there is Haiku, the lightweight model. Use Haiku when speed matters more than depth. It is useful for quick summaries, simple rewrites, classification, routing or high volume tasks where you do not need deep reasoning. Then there is Opus. Opus 5 is the deeper reasoning model built for complex enterprise work and long horizon agentic tasks. As Anthropic stated, it is particularly strong at checking and correcting its own work. Use it when the work is harder, messier or higher stakes. For example, a strategic decision, a complex financial analysis, a sensitive executive message or a multi-step task where the first answer needs to be more complete and considered. Think of it as the specialist you bring in when Sonnet's first pass is not enough. Start with high effort and only move higher for genuinely demanding work. Lower effort can still produce strong results with less time and usage. Finally, there is Fable. Fable 5 is Anthropic's most powerful model. It was recently released more broadly after being paused for safety updates. It is built for hard thinking tasks and for AI systems that can plan and carry out many steps over time. For example, it can research a topic, create a plan, write documents, improve them based on feedback and manage tasks across tools with little human help. However, as the most capable model, Fable 5 will draw down your usage much faster than Opus 4.8. So it is best suited for teams building serious AI systems rather than most daily individual tasks. Now, where do you find and switch these models? To switch models, start a new chat and click the model name in the right corner of the prompt box. That opens the model picker where you'll see your available options. You'll also notice the effort options from the model selection dropdown. This lets you decide how much effort Claude should put into a response. Keep in mind, the higher the effort, the slower the response and the faster the credits run out. So how should you choose? Use Haiku when the task is simple and speed matters. Use Sonnet for most daily work, drafting, planning, summarizing, analysis, coding and working with documents. Use Opus when the task needs deeper judgment or a stronger first pass. Use Fable when you are building with the API, working with very long context or designing a long-running, agentic workflow. Sonnet 5 is available across all plans and is the default for Freedom Pro. Opus 5 is available on paid plans with usage limits depending on the plan. Because it uses more compute than Sonnet, it will draw down your allowance faster, especially at higher effort settings. Claude Fable 5 is also not on the free tier and with capped usage at a maximum of 50% of a user's weekly subscription limit, depending on your specific account tier. So keep in mind, the model you pick shapes the result before you write a single word. Start making that distinction today and you'll get more out of Claude.
